paragraphs: On Friday, Mia read an email from her pen pal, Nadia. "Please send me a photo of a wild animal," Nadia wrote. Mia smiled, because she wanted to be a wildlife photographer. The next morning, the Explorers were going to the nature park. That evening, Mia packed her camera and a small notebook. She also put out comfortable shoes for the walk. She wanted to send Nadia a very good photo.

First, the club took the bus to the park on Saturday morning. Everybody wore comfortable shoes, and Mia held her camera. Then they stopped at the small store near the gate. Teacher Kim bought cold water for everyone. Ranger Mark was there with a green cap and a big smile. "Today, we will walk slowly and quietly," he said. "Then we can see the wildlife."

After that, the group walked along a path under tall trees. The sun was warm, but the trees gave shade. Mia saw a variety of birds. Some were small and blue, and some were big and white. She took ten photos, but they were not very good. The birds flew away too fast. "Wait for the right moment," said Ranger Mark. "A good photographer can wait." Mia waited, and she did not move.

Then something small moved on a rock. It was a green lizard, and it looked at the camera. Mia took a photo very slowly. The lizard did not run away, and Mia was very happy. "Do you know a fact about lizards?" asked Ranger Mark. "No, I do not," said Mia. "Some lizards can drop their tails and grow a new one," he said. Mia wrote the fact in her notebook.

In the evening, Mia looked at all her photos on the computer. She chose the lizard photo, because it was the best one. Finally, she wrote an email to Nadia. "Here is a wild animal from our nature park," she wrote. "A lizard can grow a new tail!" Nadia wrote back, "I love it. Please send more photos!" Mia smiled at her notebook, and she planned the next trip.
